mka-handshake.pcap: A MN=1 hello (claim Key Server, no peers yet)
B MN=1 hello (saw A; Potential Peer List; not Key Server)
A MN=2 Key Server: Live Peer List + Distributed SAK + SAK Use (tx)
B MN=2: Live Peer List + SAK Use (tx+rx) after installing SAK
A MN=3: both sides using SAK (tx+rx), session up
mka-after-eap.pcap: EAP-Success (Authenticator → Supplicant; MSK already on both sides)
Authenticator MN=1 hello (claim Key Server, no peers yet)
Supplicant MN=1 hello (saw Authenticator; Potential Peer List; not Key Server)
Authenticator MN=2 Key Server: Live Peer List + Distributed SAK + SAK Use (tx)
Supplicant MN=2: Live Peer List + SAK Use (tx+rx) after installing SAK
Authenticator MN=3: both sides using SAK (tx+rx), session up
mka-rekey.pcap: A MN=4 keepalive on SAK#1 (steady state, AN=0 KN=1)
A→B data PN=10 AN=0 with SAK#1 (PN keeps climbing toward exhaustion)
A MN=5 rekey: Distributed SAK#2 (AN=1 KN=2) + SAK Use latest=AN1 tx / old=AN0 tx+rx
B MN=5 installed SAK#2: SAK Use latest=AN1 tx+rx / old=AN0 tx+rx
A MN=6 stopped tx on SAK#1: latest=AN1 tx+rx / old=AN0 rx-only (drain)
A→B data PN=1 AN=1 with SAK#2 — PN restarts at 1 (each direction is its own SA with a fresh replay window)
B→A data PN=1 AN=1 with SAK#2 — PN restarts at 1 (each direction is its own SA with a fresh replay window)
B MN=7 keepalive on SAK#2; old SA retired (old KN=0)
mka-co30.pcap: A MN=8: Distributed SAK#3 with confidentiality offset code 1 (=30 octets, AN=2 KN=3)
A→B data PN=1 AN=2 co=30 with SAK#3 — inner EtherType+IPv4+8 octets travel in clear (still ICV-protected), only the payload is encrypted
B→A data PN=1 AN=2 co=30 with SAK#3 — inner EtherType+IPv4+8 octets travel in clear (still ICV-protected), only the payload is encrypted
B MN=8 keepalive: SAK Use latest=AN2 tx+rx (installed SAK#3)
mka-xpn.pcap: A MN=9 (MKA version 3, 802.1X-2020) rekey to XPN suite: Distributed SAK#4 carries cipher suite 00-80-C2-00-01-00-00-03 (body length 36; default suite omits the ID, 28)
B MN=9 installed XPN SAK#4: SAK Use latest=AN3 tx+rx; peer-list byte now carries B's own SSCI LSB 0x01 (非 XPN 故事里是 0)
A→B PN64=0x1FFFFFFFF: the LAST frame of the first 2^32 epoch — a 32-bit suite would have to rekey here, XPN keeps going
A→B PN64=0x200000001: on-wire PN wrapped to 0x00000001; receiver recovers the high half from SA state (802.1AE 10.6), same SAK, no MKA churn
B→A PN64=0x100000003: own SA, own SSCI, own PN64 space — the nonce is per-SC
B MN=10 keepalive on the XPN SA: everything above 2^32 is business as usual
mka-multi-peer.pcap: A MN=1 hello (Key Server claim, prio 16 — smallest priority wins)
B MN=1 hello (Potential Peer List: A; prio 32)
C MN=1 hello (Potential Peer List: A + B; prio 48 — three members, one CAK/CKN)
A MN=2 Key Server: ONE Distributed SAK for the whole CA + SAK Use (tx) + Live Peer List with TWO tuples
B MN=2: SAK Use tx+rx (installed the SAK); Live Peer List [A, C]
C MN=2: SAK Use tx+rx; Live Peer List [A, B]
A MN=3: SAK Use tx+rx — all three members live on the single SAK
A→B data PN=1 AN=0 SC=1 ICMP seq=20 — node-a's own SC/SCI; explicit SCI because the CA has more than two members
B→C data PN=1 AN=0 SC=1 ICMP seq=21 — node-b's own SC/SCI; explicit SCI because the CA has more than two members
C→A data PN=1 AN=0 SC=1 ICMP seq=22 — node-c's own SC/SCI; explicit SCI because the CA has more than two members
C MN=3 keepalive: one CAK, one KS, one SAK, three unidirectional SCs
macsec-replay.pcap: A→B PN=1 — in order, accepted; window advances
A→B PN=3 — in order, accepted (remember this frame)
A→B PN=5 — PN=4 missing (lost/reordered); PN=5 accepted, window slides: floor is now PN=3
A→B PN=4 arrives late — inside the window (floor=3 < 4 < next=6), accepted as reordered
REPLAY of frame 3, byte-identical, ICV still verifies — DROPPED: PN=3 <= floor(3), below the replay window
DUPLICATE of the previous frame — DROPPED: PN=6 already seen inside the window
A→B PN=7 — in order, accepted; the replay attempts never advanced the window
session-full.pcap: A MN=1 hello (claim Key Server, no peers yet)
B MN=1 hello (saw A; Potential Peer List; not Key Server)
A MN=2 Key Server: Live Peer List + Distributed SAK + SAK Use (tx)
B MN=2: Live Peer List + SAK Use (tx+rx) after installing SAK
A MN=3: both sides using SAK (tx+rx), session up
